subject: Recap & next steps: FinWise performance SLOs and load test
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Greene <samantha@finwise.com>, Tom Li <tom.li@finwise.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-20T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap & next steps: FinWise performance SLOs and load test

Thanks again for the call today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the customer-led load test.

Key SLOs we discussed:
- Latency: p95 <= 300ms for non-streaming generation (prompt+response).
- Throughput: baseline target 500 requests/sec sustained for 10 minutes; burst up to 800 rps for short periods.
- Concurrency: aim to support 200 concurrent sessions (each session may issue streaming requests).
- Streaming: support chunked streaming with final token latency target p95 <= 150ms after stream start; preserve ordering and partial-output semantics.

Load test coordination items (actionable):
1) Test window: customer-led run preferred — proposed initial window: 2027-03-24 02:00–06:00 UTC (please confirm).
2) Scripts: attaching a k6 script prototype (k6-script-v1.js) and a Locust scenario (locustfile.py) for your team to run. Please adapt user journeys to match production shapes (avg prompt length, streaming vs non-streaming split ~60/40).
3) Test accounts & credentials: we will provision a test API key and a sandbox account for FinWise.
4) IP allowlist: please provide egress IPs from your test runners so we can whitelist them on our side; temporary test IPs for Redwood runners are: 52.23.45.67, 34.201.100.12 (we recommend you whitelist these if you plan to pull data from our test endpoints).
5) Warmup & cache: include a 10–15 minute warmup to populate KV/prefix caches; otherwise first-wave latencies will be higher.
6) Metrics & reporting: please share raw k6/Locust results and the timeseries for error rates, p50/p95/p99 latencies, and throughput. We will correlate with our server-side traces.

Attachments: k6-script-v1.js, locustfile.py, loadtest-plan.pdf (attached).

Next steps: can you confirm the test window and share the egress IPs + preferred contact during the run? We can provide a live Slack channel and a small on-call rotation from Redwood to help during the window.

Best,
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

---
From: Samantha Greene <samantha@finwise.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Li <tom.li@finwise.com>
Date: 2027-03-20T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: FinWise performance SLOs and load test

Thanks Logan — this looks good and covers everything we discussed. A couple of quick notes:
- The proposed SLOs look reasonable; we may need to revisit p95 targets depending on streaming behavior.
- Test window: would it be possible to move the window 2 hours earlier to 2027-03-24 00:00–04:00 UTC? Our ops team prefers that slot to avoid business hours overlap.
- We will be running k6 from our CI runners but can also execute Locust from a dedicated EC2 if needed. I will confirm which runner we use by EOD.

Can you attach the temporary test API key in a follow-up (masked in email, full key via your secure channel)? Also can you share a short network diagram or which endpoints we should hit?

Appreciate it — Samantha
Samantha Greene
Head of Platform Engineering, FinWise
S: +1 (212) 555-0123

---
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Greene <samantha@finwise.com>, Tom Li <tom.li@finwise.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-20T17:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: FinWise performance SLOs and load test

Thanks — we can accommodate the earlier window. Confirmed: 2027-03-24 00:00–04:00 UTC as the run window.

Temporary test credentials (partial, will send full securely):
- Test account: finwise-loadtest@test.redwood.ai
- API key (masked): sk-test-XXXXXXabcd (full key will be pushed to your vault via our Secrets share; if you prefer we can use a DocuSign-like secure link).

Endpoints to hit (v1):
- https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate (standard gen endpoint)
- https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/stream (streaming endpoint)

I've attached a short network diagram and an updated loadtest-plan.pdf which calls out warmup sequencing and a recommended mix: 60% non-streaming, 40% streaming (short-latency checks + long-stream sampling).

Attachments: locustfile.py, loadtest-plan.pdf

We will add your egress IPs to our allowlist once you share them; if you prefer, you can also point at the Redwood runners above (we recommend whitelisting both directions for the first run).

Logan

---
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-21T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: FinWise performance SLOs and load test

Quick internal note — please ask FinWise to include a dedicated streaming-heavy scenario that keeps an open connection for ~60s and emits tokens at their production cadence. We want to measure incremental CPU and KV cache behavior during active streams. Also recommend a 15-minute warmup for cache and compile-steps on the model.

I'll plan to join the run window and watch tracing; flag me if you want me to kick off any on-call investigations.

-Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

---
From: Samantha Greene <samantha@finwise.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: FinWise performance SLOs and load test

Confirmed on our side: we will run the k6 script from our dedicated EC2 runner during 2027-03-24 00:00–04:00 UTC.

Egress IPs (please whitelist): 3.120.45.88, 3.120.45.89
We will run the following scenarios:
- scenario A: non-streaming gen (60% traffic), target 500 rps sustained for 10m
- scenario B: streaming sessions (40% traffic), 200 concurrent sessions, each streaming for ~60s

We will share raw k6 outputs and Grafana links after the run. Please provide the secure API key delivery and Slack channel invite for the run. If we see sustained errors >1% or p95 spikes >500ms we will pause and coordinate.

Thanks — Samantha
